chunk_findings.detail:
`_row` is the shared row builder used by every list surface (`task list`, `bug list`, `phase list`, `research list`, `lesson list`, and the MCP `ddflow_list`/CLI twin this change adds). The new keys are materialised unconditionally for **all** record kinds:

```python
"parent": it.parent or "",
"needs": list(it.needs),
"globs": list(it.globs),
```

`parent` is written defensively (`or ""`), which shows these optional plan fields are not guaranteed to be populated on a record; `needs`/`globs` get no such handling. Two concrete inputs break:

- A record with the field unset/`None` (e.g. a bug or research note that has no declared files, since the README itself scopes `parent`/`needs`/`globs` to "a task or phase row"): `list(None)` raises `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable`, so the previously-working `ddflow bug list --json` (and `ddflow list bug --json`) now crashes in the row builder rather than returning rows.
- A record where the value is still the raw scalar from the record source: `list("src/**")` / `list("T-1,T-2")` silently yields one element per *character* (`['s','r','c',...]`), i.e. `--json` no longer carries "the declared files"/edges the docstring promises. Note that `tags` is deliberately normalised through the `_tags(it.tags, cfg)` helper for exactly this reason; `needs`/`globs` bypass any normalisation.

Either way the value should be coerced defensively (e.g. `list(it.needs or ())`, and via a normaliser if the field can be a scalar) before being emitted for every kind.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/viewers.py:97-99 (`_row`, new `needs`/`globs` keys)

chunk_findings.detail: The snapshot shows the newly added subcommand's usage as `ddflow list [-h] [--state STATE] ... [--item ITEM] {task,phase,bug,research,lesson}`. The braces are *not* wrapped in `[...]`, so argparse treats the kind as a **required** positional. Consequently the exact command from the bug report and from the stated expected outcome — `ddflow list` — still raises an argparse error (`the following arguments are required: {task,phase,bug,research,lesson}`) instead of listing the queue or pointing at `board --json`. The regression the change claims to fix ("Expected: 'ddflow list' ... or a pointer to the equivalent") is therefore only satisfied when the user already knows to append one of `task/phase/bug/research/lesson`; the bare invocation that the report calls out as broken remains broken. If the intent was that a kind be optional (defaulting to, say, `task`), the positional must be declared with `nargs='?'` (or a default), which would render as `[{task,phase,bug,research,lesson}]` in this snapshot.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_cli_help.ambr (snapshot `test_help[ddflow list]`, usage line)

chunk_findings.detail: `_union_params` dedupes on the flag name with `seen.setdefault(p.name, p)`, so the `list` command keeps the *first* `Param` object seen for a name and silently discards every later definition from the other kinds — including that Param's `choices`, `default` and `type`. The resulting parser is therefore an arbitrary kind's parser for each shared flag. The flags whose definitions are most likely to differ per kind are exactly the state vocabularies: the README in this same diff documents `ddflow bug list --state invalid` and `ddflow research list --state refuted` (per-kind states), while the union is built in `_LISTS` order and so takes whichever kind comes first (task). Given `ddflow list bug --state invalid`, argparse is left enforcing the first kind's `choices` and rejects `invalid` before any handler runs, even though the `<kind> list` form the README claims parity with accepts it — so "the same reader with the kind as a word" is not true for the kinds whose flag definitions were dropped. The same mechanism means any flag a kind lacks is now accepted at parse time for that kind (`--owner` on a kind whose reader has no owner filter), and since the union is the command's declared param set, nothing in this change implements the "refused by the engine" the comment relies on; the selected kind's reader only consults its own `_filter_params(kind)`, so such a flag is silently ignored and the caller gets unfiltered rows instead of the error the docstring promises. Unioning names without unioning/validating the definitions is the defect; e.g. `ddflow list bug --state invalid` fails while `ddflow bug list --state invalid` succeeds, and `ddflow list lesson --owner me` reports unfiltered lessons.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:_union_params (line ~176)

chunk_findings.detail: The new `list` subcommand declares `{task,phase,bug,research,lesson}` as a **required** positional: the usage line renders it without the surrounding `[...]` brackets that argparse emits for `nargs='?'`, and the body lists it under "positional arguments" with no default marker. Consequently the exact input from the bug report, `ddflow list`, does not succeed — it now exits with `the following arguments are required: {task,phase,bug,research,lesson}`. The stated expectation for this fix is that the CLI and MCP surfaces match (`ddflow list`, cf. MCP `ddflow_list`) or that the user is pointed at the equivalent (`board --json`); the bare invocation does neither, it just replaces the old `invalid choice: list … Did you mean split?` error with a different argparse error for the same repro. If the intent was for `ddflow list` to list the queue (as the docs/skills do) with `task/phase/bug/...` as optional filters, the positional needs `nargs='?'` (which would render as `[{task,phase,bug,research,lesson}]` in this snapshot); if the intent was the bare form to be rejected, it should at least redirect to the equivalent command rather than emit a required-argument error.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_cli_help.ambr (snapshot `test_help[ddflow list]`, usage line)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard uses "the attribute value is truthy" as a proxy for "the user passed this flag", which is wrong for flags that take falsy but meaningful values. In Python `0 == False` and `"" == ""`, so the tuple membership test `value not in (None, False, "")` returns False for `0` and `""`, and `stray` stays empty. Concrete repro: `--limit` is a filter param of some other kind but is accepted by the union parser of `list`. Running `ddflow list task --limit 0` yields `getattr(a, "limit") == 0`, the `not in (None, False, "")` check is False, `stray` is `[]`, and the function falls through to `cmd_list` — exactly the silently-ignored-flag behavior this change is supposed to refuse. The same happens for `ddflow list task --status ""` (empty string), which is accepted while `ddflow list task --status open` is refused, and if the downstream reader tests for `is not None` (typical for numeric limits/slices) it can silently change results instead of erroring. The check needs to compare against the argparse default per param (or check whether the flag appears in `sys.argv`), not test the value for truthiness.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:173 (the `getattr(...) not in (None, False, "")` predicate in `cmd_list_any`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The guard decides whether a flag "was supplied" by comparing the parsed value against the literal tuple `(None, False, "")` instead of checking whether the option was actually present on the command line, and that test is not equivalent to "unset". Two concrete failure modes follow:

- False negative (guard silently skipped): any union param that is not owned by the kind but takes a value can still be passed with a value equal to one of those literals. For example, if `--phase` is a union filter that `task` does not declare, then `ddflow list task --phase ""` sets `a.phase = ""`, the condition `getattr(a, "phase", None) not in (None, False, "")` is `False`, the `stray` list stays empty, and the command falls through to `cmd_list` and exits 0 — silently accepting exactly the unsupported flag this code is supposed to refuse (and `--all`'s test only passes because `--all` is a `store_true` that becomes `True`). The same hole applies to any value that compares equal to `False`/`None`/`""`.

- False positive (guard fires with no user input): the tuple does not cover empty containers. A param declared in the union with `action="append"` and the common `default=[]` yields `getattr(a, p.name)` == `[]`, for which `[] in (None, False, "")` is `False`, so `[] not in (...)` is `True` and it is reported as stray even though the user typed nothing. If any such param exists, every `ddflow list <kind>` for a kind that does not own it returns `REFUSED` (3) instead of listing — breaking the existing happy-path test (`assert code == 0 and "P1" in out`).

A check based on actual presence (sentinel default / `argparse` `default=SUPPRESS`, or scanning the argv for the option) or a plain truthiness test `if p.name not in own and getattr(a, p.name, None):` avoids both.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:176 (stray detection in `cmd_list_any`)
